transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-24 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (Summit Head of ML), Evan Brooks (Summit CTO), Rita Gomez (Infra)

Summary:
Redwood did a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating tradeoffs between hosted API and Dedicated capacity for low-latency storefront features. Security and KMS for PII is a blocker; they requested SOC2 docs and pilot benchmarks. Next steps agreed: pricing + security docs, pilot schedule, route CSV.

Topics:
- Console: per-route dashboards, token-level cost, top-k routes by spend
- Alerts and data retention for quality monitoring
- Dedicated vs hosted economics and autoscaling policies
- Pilot scope and benchmark plan
- Security: KMS, VPC, audit logs, SSO

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we have about 45 minutes, we'll walk through the console and then leave time for questions. Miguel and I will tag-team the demo. Sana, Evan, Rita, thanks for the time.
[00:18] Sana: Yep thanks. We mainly want to see per-route cost breakdowns and how we can control spend at the route level — our marketing chatbot is blowing past the forecast.
[00:30] Miguel: Totally, we'll start in the Usage Analytics tab. There are two main views: top-level spend and per-route dashboards. Quick note, some labels in the console are abbreviate, so please tell us if anything looks off.
[01:05] Miguel: (screen share) Here is the per-route table — you can filter by model, deployment (hosted vs dedicated), region, and time window. The cost column is token-based and we also show inferred inference compute cost and estimated network egress.
[01:30] Evan: How accurate is the compute estimate? Our CFO wants to reconcile with cloud bills.
[01:40] Avery: Good question — the console shows a unit economics breakdown: tokens, decode/compute cycles (estimated), and a normalized cost column. For Dedicated we use committed GPU unit pricing which maps to your reserved commit; for hosted we use published per-token rates. The compute estimate is based on token counts plus model profile heuristics — it's within 5-15% in our internal benchmarks but we can run a pilot to align to your cloud billing.
[02:15] Sana: Can you show the route-level detail — like top 10 routes by spend and per-call P50/P95 latency?
[02:25] Miguel: Sure — switching to the route dashboard for the 'product_search' route — you can see throughput, latency histograms, token distribution, and cost per-call. There's also a cost trend sparkline. Note underneath we surface suggestions from Redwood Optimize: batching windows and cache hints.
[03:05] Rita: That cache hint — is that prefix/KV cache? We run a lot of repeated product queries.
[03:15] Miguel: Yes, prefix and KV cache. The suggestions show estimated cost savings if you enable 30s prefix caching or apply a 256-token KV cache warm strategy. We provide simulated savings assuming your traffic mix.
[03:35] Evan: If we enable caching, how does that interact with latency SLOs and freshness of results? Some of our product data updates quickly.
[03:45] Avery: The suggestions include TTL knobs and invalidation policies. You can set route-level freshness thresholds; the console will estimate the percent of requests impacted. For highly dynamic routes you might choose smaller TTL or bypass cache for write-heavy paths.
[04:10] Sana: Can we allocate different models per route? For example, a cheaper 2B quantized model for autocomplete and larger model for checkout chat.
[04:20] Miguel: Yup — the routing rules in the console let you pin model variants to routes, and you can set fallbacks. The per-route cost will reflect the model mix. We also show an estimated quality delta if you pick a smaller model (based on prior evals) so you can trade off cost vs summary quality.
[04:50] Sana: Nice. Show me how alerts work — we need to be notified if cost spikes on a route.
[05:00] Miguel: Alerts are coupled to the dashboards. You can create an alert on spend/day or per-route spend rate. We also have anomaly detection that flags unexpected token surges; it auto-suggests a temporary throttle policy or fallback to a cheaper model.
[05:30] Rita: For Dedicated, what's the burst behavior? If we commit to N GPUs but traffic spikes, will Redwood autoscale?
[05:45] Avery: Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies. You define a baseline commit and a burst pool you can tap into. The console has a policy editor where you set scale triggers (CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, latency). There's also an automated fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is exhausted.
[06:20] Evan: Ok security stuff — we need KMS support and audit logs. Is the console's data surfaced to Redwood? We want zero plaintext token storage in hosted mode.
[06:35] Miguel: We have multiple options. Hosted: we retain short-term telemetry but not customer PII; you can opt for no retention. Dedicated and Private: telemetry stays in your VPC, and you can integrate your KMS/HSM. We surface audit logs (API calls, rollouts, access) and you can forward to your SIEM. We'll send the SOC 2 pack and the KMS integration guide after the call.
[07:10] Sana: Do you support SSO/SAML for RBAC? We need scoped roles for data access.
[07:20] Avery: Yes, SSO + SCIM provisioning, role based access, and route-level RBAC are supported in Dedicated/Private and for hosted enterprise accounts.
[07:35] Rita: Great. Back to cost — show a breakdown by token type: prompt vs completion vs embeddings?
[07:45] Miguel: The analytics show prompt vs completion tokens and embeddings separately. In the token-level drill-down we show average prompt length, average completion length, and the per-token cost. There's also a per-route heatmap for cost contributors.
[08:15] Evan: How do you handle function/tool calling and streaming when calculating cost?
[08:25] Miguel: Streaming is billed as tokens emitted; function/tool calls that generate structured output are charged like any completion. For complex tool chains we recommend measuring the end-to-end token footprint in pilot benchmarks — the console will attribute tokens to routes, even if you do fan-out to multiple tool endpoints.
[08:55] Sana: If we want to cap spend per route monthly, can we enforce that?
[09:05] Miguel: Yes — the quota engine can enforce soft limits (alerts + throttles) or hard caps (block calls). You can set per-route daily/monthly quotas and specify failover behavior (return 429 or fallback to cached result).
[09:30] Sana: Perfect. Can you customize the dashboard tiles? We want a route tile for checkout with specific KPIs.
[09:40] Miguel: Dashboard builder supports custom tiles with KPIs you choose — latency P95, cost per 1k calls, error rate, and any custom tag you emit.
[09:55] Evan: On tags — how do we tag requests? We have middleware in our API.
[10:05] Miguel: You can send metadata headers; they become facets in the analytics engine. We also support sampling and payload scrubbing to avoid capturing sensitive content.
[10:25] Rita: Is there any correlation between tokenization changes and historical data? We're worried a tokenizer update will shift per-token counts.
[10:35] Avery: We version tokenizer profiles per model. The console lets you view historical tokenization deltas when you change model variants. For accounting we show a normalized token column to help compare across model versions.
[10:55] Sana: Let's talk pilot: we want a 1-week benchmark against our production traffic for product_search and checkout_chat. What would you need?
[11:05] Miguel: We'll need a route CSV with peak QPS, 95th latency goals, current model mapping, and a sample request set (anonymized). We'll run a pilot with a mirror of traffic or replay, measure token usage, latency, and then produce a per-route cost projection. We can also run a Dedicated sizing recommendation if you prefer a reserved commit.
[11:35] Evan: For the trial, will you run in our VPC or use Redwood hosted?
[11:45] Avery: We can do both; in most pilots we run in Redwood hosted with secure telemetry options. For higher security requirements, we can run the pilot inside your VPC via a private connector. We'll match the approach to your security posture.
[12:05] Sana: About rollouts — can we do canary/A-B and automatic rollback if we see quality regressions?
[12:15] Miguel: Yes — the rollout engine supports canary percentages and automated rollback triggers tied to quality monitors. You can upload prompt sets and expected outputs; if eval metrics degrade beyond thresholds we auto-rollback.
[12:40] Rita: That eval integration sounds useful. Does the console keep the prompt set private?
[12:50] Avery: Prompt sets are part of the customer's workspace; in Hosted we store them with redaction options, in Dedicated/Private they can remain in your environment.
[13:05] Sana: Can we map cost to product teams? We have multiple teams using the same account.
[13:15] Miguel: You can enforce tagging at the request level and the analytics let you group by team. We also have chargeback reports that export CSV per-team per-month.
[13:35] Evan: Any native integration with our billing system?
[13:40] Avery: We support billing exports and a billing API to pull usage by tag. Many customers ingest CSV into their FinOps tooling.
[13:55] Sana: Ok I'm convinced the console surface is solid. A couple of specific concerns: 1) We're sensitive about PII being logged in hosted mode and 2) We need guarantees on latency for peak hours.
[14:10] Miguel: For PII, options: a) disable full payload logging and only log metadata, b) token redaction, c) Private deployment. For latency, Dedicated with pinned GPUs and performance SLOs is the path — we can model expected P95 given your QPS and sequence lengths in the pilot.
[14:35] Evan: On pricing — is there a simple way to see the delta between running hosted vs Dedicated in terms of $/1M requests?
[14:45] Avery: The console's cost simulator can show per-route scenarios: choose hosted or dedicated, input commit size, expected QPS, and it outputs per-request and monthly cost. We'll attach the simulator outputs to your pilot report.
[15:05] Sana: Do you support quantized model variants in Dedicated? We prefer 4-bit quantization for cost reasons.
[15:15] Miguel: Yes, Dedicated supports quantized variants and we can recommend quantization profile per workload via Redwood Optimize. The console will show expected latency and accuracy deltas.
[15:35] Rita: Can we do a hard cap on Dedicated spend if something goes wrong with autoscale?
[15:45] Avery: For Dedicated, your commit defines baseline spend; we can set guardrails on burst consumption and alert finance if burst crosses thresholds. For absolute hard caps you'd rely on policy that prevents additional GPUs from being provisioned — we can set that.
[16:05] Evan: Good. Any compliance paperwork we should read now?
[16:10] Miguel: We'll push SOC 2, ISO, and data processing addendum. Expect the pack within 24-48 hours.
[16:20] Sana: Great. Couple more small items — can the console show long tail routes (less than 1% traffic) so we can triage?
[16:30] Miguel: There's a long-tail report that surfaces routes by spend and latency then clusters infrequent routes for review. Very handy for debugging ad-hoc endpoints.
[16:45] Rita: One operational question — how do you handle model updates and KV cache migrations?
[16:55] Miguel: We surface migration guides. For KV caches, the runtime has a warmed cache migration that can prepopulate keys for new model variants; for model updates we support staged rollouts with cache warming windows.
[17:15] Evan: OK let's recap next steps and owners.
[17:20] Avery: Recap — I'll send pricing deck + Dedicated pricing spreadsheet; Miguel will share pilot checklist and sample load scripts; Rita will share route CSV and sample anonymized requests. We'll aim to run the pilot week of 2026-12-01. We'll also share SOC2 and KMS docs.
[17:45] Sana: Thanks all. Looking forward to the pilot.
[17:50] Miguel: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts.
[17:55] (call ends)
